answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by making every fresh identity post a unique bond that only unlocks after a quorum of established peers mirrors its work: each task's output is hashed into a per-operator juniper ledger, and any duplicate submissions traced to one wallet forfeit the whole cluster's stake. Reaching the reputation zenith then demands long stretches of real, non-duplicated output, so renting a thousand throwaway accounts costs more in bonding than the emission it could farm.
